{{< include _workflow.qmd >}}

> These notes teach you to analyse playtest data in R: to plan a playtest, describe
> what happened, decide whether a difference between builds is real, and write it up
> as a finding a designer can act on. They assume **no statistics and no R**. They
> do assume you build games, and every example comes from one playtest of one game,
> *Tidebreak*. Read this page first; it takes five minutes.

## What You Are Learning

Three weeks, one question at a time:

- **Week 1: what happened?** Plan a playtest, read the data into R, and describe it
  honestly: centre, spread, shape, and the players at the edges.
- **Week 2: is it real?** Clean the raw export, then decide whether a difference
  between two builds is more than chance, and whether it is big enough to matter.
- **Week 3: what does it mean?** Relate variables to each other without confusing
  association with cause, draw figures for other people, and write the report.

Every analysis in these notes follows the same **analytical workflow**. The strip at
the top of each page shows where that page sits in it:

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-workflow
%%| fig-cap: "The analytical workflow. Every notes page covers one or two of these steps."
flowchart LR
  A["Ask a design<br/>question"] --> B["Collect<br/>data"]
  B --> C["Inspect<br/>and clean"]
  C --> D["Visualise"]
  D --> E["Describe"]
  E --> F["Quantify<br/>uncertainty"]
  F --> G["Test a<br/>hypothesis"]
  G --> H["Consider<br/>confounds"]
  H --> I["Interpret"]
  I --> J["Report"]
  classDef s fill:#f8f9fa,stroke:#6c757d,color:#212529
  class A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I,J s
```

The R work inside it follows the **R analysis cycle**. The middle is a loop, not a
line: you transform, look, model and look again.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-r-cycle
%%| fig-cap: "The R analysis cycle. Import and tidy once; transform, visualise and model in a loop; communicate at the end."
flowchart LR
  I["Import<br/>read_csv()"] --> T["Tidy<br/>pivot_longer()"]
  T --> X["Transform<br/>filter(), mutate()"]
  X --> V["Visualise<br/>hist(), ggplot()"]
  V --> M["Model<br/>t.test(), lm()"]
  M --> X
  V --> X
  M --> C["Communicate<br/>Quarto report"]
  classDef s fill:#f8f9fa,stroke:#6c757d,color:#212529
  classDef e fill:#fbeaea,stroke:#b22222,color:#212529
  class I,T,X,V,M s
  class C e
```

## The Three-Week Route

Each class is two 90-minute cycles: a framing question, about 30 minutes of
theory from the notes, a 15-minute demo, then the lab. The notes hold more than one
theory slot can cover; the class covers each page's core, and the rest is for
reading afterwards.

| When | In class | Read before or after | Lab | Demo |
| :- | :- | :- | :- | :- |
| **Before Week 1** | | [R from First Principles](02-r-first-principles.qmd) | [Lab 00](../labs/setting-up.qmd) | |
| **Week 1, cycle 1** | [Planning a Playtest](01-planning-a-playtest.qmd), [Data, Variables and Types](03-data-and-types.qmd) | | [Lab 01](../labs/reading-data.qmd) Part A | [Week 1](../demos/week-1.qmd) |
| **Week 1, cycle 2** | [Describing Variables](04-describing-variables.qmd), [Distributions and Shape](05-distributions-and-shape.qmd) | Going further sections | [Lab 01](../labs/reading-data.qmd) Part B | [Week 1](../demos/week-1.qmd) |
| **Week 2, cycle 1** | [Cleaning and Transforming](06-cleaning-and-transforming.qmd) | | [Lab 02](../labs/comparing-builds.qmd) Part A | [Week 2](../demos/week-2.qmd) |
| **Week 2, cycle 2** | [Comparing Groups](08-comparing-groups.qmd), with the simulations from [From Sample to Population](07-sample-to-population.qmd) | [From Sample to Population](07-sample-to-population.qmd) in full | [Lab 02](../labs/comparing-builds.qmd) Part B | [Week 2](../demos/week-2.qmd) |
| **Week 3, cycle 1** | [Visualising with ggplot2](09-visualising-with-ggplot2.qmd), [Relationships](10-relationships-and-regression.qmd) | The regression section | [Lab 03](../labs/complete-analysis.qmd) Part A | [Week 3](../demos/week-3.qmd) |
| **Week 3, cycle 2** | [Interpreting and Reporting Evidence](11-reporting-evidence.qmd) | | [Lab 03](../labs/complete-analysis.qmd) Part B | [Week 3](../demos/week-3.qmd) |

**Base R first, then the tidyverse.** Weeks 1 and 2 draw every plot with base R
(`hist()`, `boxplot()`, `plot()`), the quick plots you make while thinking. Week 3
introduces `ggplot2` for figures other people will read. The same order runs
through the data handling: `tapply()` before `group_by()`. The reason is in
[R from First Principles](02-r-first-principles.qmd#base-r-first-then-the-tidyverse).

## How a Notes Page Works

Every notes page has the same shape, so you always know where to look.

| Part | What it is for |
| :- | :- |
| **Opening quote** | What the page is for, and the playtest question running through it |
| **At a glance** | Time, what to read first, key terms, the R it introduces |
| **Why This Matters** | Why a games team needs the idea at all |
| **Core sections** | One idea each: a plain-English definition, a figure, the *Tidebreak* example, the R, how you would say it in a report, and the common mistake |
| **Going further** | Collapsed boxes with extra depth, including "The maths, if you want it". Never needed for the labs |
| **Quick check** | A collapsed question to test yourself mid-page |
| **Worked Example** | The page's question answered step by step, usually overturning the obvious answer |
| **Interpretation Guidance** | What the data shows, what it suggests, and what can legitimately be concluded |
| **Common Mistakes** | The errors that turn up in real reports |
| **Practice** | Short exercises with collapsed answers: predict, compute, critique, decide |
| **Summary and Key Terms** | The page in a few lines, and a glossary for revision |

**Every number is computed.** Each number in the prose is calculated from the data
when the page is built, so it cannot be out of date or mistyped. Figures stamped
*Illustration* use simulated data to show an idea cleanly; everything else is
*Tidebreak*.

**Code is there to be typed.** Every chunk runs as shown, provided the data sits in
the `data/` folder of your project. Typing it, rather than copying it, is how it
sticks.

---

## The Labs and Reference Pages

**Four labs**: a setup lab, then one lab per week in two parts, matching the
week's two cycles. Exercises are tagged by what they ask of you:

| Tier | What it asks | Time |
| :- | :- | :- |
| `[Do]` | One function, one result | 2–3 minutes |
| `[Apply]` | Combine two or three ideas | 5 minutes |
| `[Decide]` | A judgement call with no single right answer | 5–8 minutes |

The `[Decide]` exercises are the ones that matter most: anyone can run a t-test, and
the module is about knowing what the result means. Solutions are in collapsed boxes;
open them after you have tried, even when your attempt worked.

**Three reference pages** for looking things up during a lab:

- [Statistics Reference](../reference/reference-statistics.qmd): every term, in
  plain English, with a *Tidebreak* example and the common mistake
- [R and Quarto Reference](../reference/r-quarto-reference.qmd): every function,
  by task
- [ggplot2 Reference](../reference/reference-ggplot2.qmd): every geometry and
  option used in Week 3

## The Game: *Tidebreak*

*Tidebreak* is a fictional four-player top-down arena game. Its playtest produced
the files every page uses:

| File | One row is | Used for |
| :- | :- | :- |
| `tidebreak_sessions.csv` | one player in one session | almost everything |
| `tidebreak_sessions_raw.csv` | the same, as exported, with faults | cleaning |
| `tidebreak_survey.csv` | one post-session survey | ratings and reporting |
| `tidebreak_paired.csv` | one player who played both builds | the paired test |
| `tidebreak_frame_times.csv` | one rendered frame | performance and tails |

The data is synthetic, but it was built so that a careful analysis finds real
findings, and several of them contradict the obvious first answer. **That is the
point.** If a result surprises you, you are probably reading the data correctly.

## Before Week 1

1. Work through [Lab 00: Setting Up](../labs/setting-up.qmd), and check that the
   test document renders.
2. Read [R from First Principles](02-r-first-principles.qmd) with R open beside you.
3. Skim the [Ten Rules](ten-rules.qmd). You will meet each of them properly later.

Then start with [Planning a Playtest](01-planning-a-playtest.qmd).
